title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR used as Charles Martel: a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries after Tours, and Frankish/generic hero alternatives were available in the editor
SALADIN used as Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi: an Ayyubid Kurdish sultan of the 1170s-80s, wrong dynasty, wrong century, wrong theatre (Levant, not Iberia/Gaul)
EL_CID used as Duke Odo of Aquitaine: an 11th-century Castilian, and ironically a figure who fought Muslim and Christian rulers in Iberia, not an 8th-century Aquitanian duke

Umayyad camp built as a stone CASTLE with 99 STONE_WALL segments, a GATE and 4 GUARD_TOWERS: Abd al-Rahman's force was a mobile raiding army with a wagon/tent laager, not a masonry fortress in the Loire valley
PIKEMAN x8 in the Frankish line: the pike square is a 14th-century development; Man-at-Arms/Spearman would have covered the 8th-century Frankish infantry adequately
CAMEL_RIDER x12 as the core of the invading force: Umayyad armies in Gaul fought as horse cavalry; camel troops are an out-of-region flourish
MONASTERY for Player Two's Muslim army: Christian monastic architecture assigned to the Umayyad camp

issues_found: Charles Martel is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero — a different, later (1066) historical figure standing in for the Frankish mayor of the palace, when a renamed generic Champion or Teutonic/Frankish hero-flagged unit was available.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN, an Ayyubid sultan of the 1180s and the wrong dynasty, religion-politics and century entirely; the victory condition literally reads 'kill Saladin'.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian, again an avoidable wrong-named hero.

Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture and unit skins are unassigned and may render as Aztec, Mongol, Japanese etc. — the one setting choice the editor makes trivially (Franks vs Saracens/Berbers) was skipped.

The Umayyad raiding force is given a CASTLE, 99 STONE_WALL segments, a GATE and 4 GUARD_TOWERs — a fortified permanent stronghold, whereas Abd al-Rahman's army was a mobile plunder column encamped in the open field.
12 CAMEL_RIDERs among the Umayyad host overstates camelry; the invaders of Gaul fought as heavy and light horse, and Berber/Arab cavalry in Iberia rode horses.
PIKEMAN (a 14th-century formation) among the 732 Frankish line, where SPEARMAN/MAN_AT_ARMS alone would have sufficed within the same engine.
The Frankish 'high ground' position is undercut by a full economic Town Center/Mill/House cluster, presenting the field army as a settled town.

Charles Martel is represented by WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR, a Norman duke of 1066 — over three centuries after Tours; a renamed generic Champion or Teutonic-style infantry hero would have been correct and was available.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN, a 12th-century Ayyubid Kurd of an entirely different polity and era than the Umayyad governor of al-Andalus.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian — wrong century and wrong realm; Odo was the Frankish/Aquitanian duke who had already fought at the Garonne.

Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Frankish and Andalusi/Berber architecture and unit availability are left to chance rather than assigned (Franks and Saracens were both available).

The Umayyad camp is built as a CASTLE with 99 STONE_WALL segments and 4 GUARD_TOWERs; Abd al-Rahman's force was a raiding army encamped in the open with a baggage/plunder train, not a stone fortress in Gaul.
12 CAMEL_RIDERs for the Umayyad host at Tours; the invading force in Aquitaine was horse cavalry, and camels are a gratuitous orientalisation given Light Cavalry/Knight substitutes exist.
PIKEMAN among the Frankish line is a Late-Medieval anachronism for 732, though within the engine's abstraction of a shield wall.
The Aquitanian ally (player THREE) fields only 15 men and three tents with no real camp presence, understating Odo's role.
